---
name: assistant

on:
  issue_comment:
    # Not `edited`: someone else with write access can edit a maintainer's
    # comment, and the author we check would still be the maintainer.
    types: [created]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  # Decides whether to run at all. No secrets and no checkout in this job.
  gate:
    if: github.event.issue.pull_request && github.event.comment.user.type == 'User'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      allowed: ${{ steps.check.outputs.allowed }}
      head_ref: ${{ steps.check.outputs.head_ref }}
    steps:
      - name: Check the commenter and the pull request
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          COMMENTER: ${{ github.event.comment.user.login }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          deny() {
            echo "::notice::Assistant not run: $1"
            echo "allowed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          }

          # `maintain` is reported as `write`, and `triage` as `read`.
          permission=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/collaborators/$COMMENTER/permission" --jq .permission)
          case "$permission" in
            admin | write) ;;
            *) deny "the commenter does not have write access" ;;
          esac

          pr=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER")
          state=$(jq -r .state <<< "$pr")
          head_repo=$(jq -r .head.repo.full_name <<< "$pr")
          head_ref=$(jq -r .head.ref <<< "$pr")

          [ "$state" = "open" ] || deny "the pull request is not open"
          # Fork code must never run next to our secrets and write token.
          [ "$head_repo" = "$REPO" ] || deny "the pull request comes from a fork"
          [ "$head_ref" != "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ] || deny "the head is the default branch"

          echo "head_ref=$head_ref" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "allowed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  assistant:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.allowed == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # One run per pull request at a time, so that pushes do not race. Set here,
    # not at workflow level, so ignored comments cannot displace a queued run.
    concurrency:
      group: assistant-${{ github.event.issue.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write # push the change
      pull-requests: read # read the pull request being worked on
    steps:
      # The token is left in the git config on purpose: the agent has to push.
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0 # zizmor: ignore[artipacked]
        with:
          ref: refs/heads/${{ needs.gate.outputs.head_ref }}
          persist-credentials: true

      - name: Run the assistant
        # TODO: pin to a full commit SHA before enabling. This step receives the
        # model API key and a write token, and a tag can be moved.
        uses: acme/coding-agent@v1
        with:
          prompt: |
            A maintainer asked for help in this comment:
            ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
            Read the repository, make the change, and push it to the branch that
            is checked out. Do not push to any other branch or tag.
        env:
          MODEL_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MODEL_API_KEY }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

content.text:
I hardened `.github/workflows/assistant.yml`, but **don't enable it on the public repo yet**: `acme/coding-agent@v1` still needs pinning to a commit SHA. The change is in your working tree, uncommitted.

## What was wrong
The most serious problem was that **anyone with a GitHub account could run it**. A comment from a stranger became the agent's instructions, with `MODEL_API_KEY` and a `write-all` token available to it. It also checked out the pull request's code, including code from forks, into that same privileged job.

## What I changed
| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| A new `gate` job checks that the commenter has admin or write access (maintain counts as write) | Only people who could push anyway can drive the agent |
| Fork PRs, closed PRs and PRs whose head is the default branch are refused | Keeps outside code away from your secrets, and keeps the agent from being pointed at `main` |
| Plain issue comments and bot comments are ignored | The workflow is for people commenting on PRs |
| The `edited` trigger is removed | Someone else with write access could edit a maintainer's comment and pass the author check |
| `write-all` became `contents: write` and `pull-requests: read`, on the agent job only | Least privilege |
| Checkout uses the PR's branch instead of `refs/pull/N/head` | The agent gets a real branch to push to, not a detached commit |
| `actions/checkout` is pinned to the SHA your `ci.yml` uses (I confirmed it is v5.0.0) | A tag can be moved |
| Added timeouts and one run per PR at a time | Limits runaway runs and push races |
| The prompt now says to push only to the checked-out branch | A guide for the agent, not an enforced limit |

## Verification

## What was wrong
The most serious problem was that **anyone with a GitHub account could run it**. A comment from a stranger became the agent's instructions, with `MODEL_API_KEY` and a `write-all` token available to it. It also checked out the pull request's code, including code from forks, into that same privileged job.

## What I changed
| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| A new `gate` job checks that the commenter has admin or write access (maintain counts as write) | Only people who could push anyway can drive the agent |
| Fork PRs, closed PRs and PRs whose head is the default branch are refused | Keeps outside code away from your secrets, and keeps the agent from being pointed at `main` |
| Plain issue comments and bot comments are ignored | The workflow is for people commenting on PRs |
| The `edited` trigger is removed | Someone else with write access could edit a maintainer's comment and pass the author check |
| `write-all` became `contents: write` and `pull-requests: read`, on the agent job only | Least privilege |
| Checkout uses the PR's branch instead of `refs/pull/N/head` | The agent gets a real branch to push to, not a detached commit |
| `actions/checkout` is pinned to the SHA your `ci.yml` uses (I confirmed it is v5.0.0) | A tag can be moved |
| Added timeouts and one run per PR at a time | Limits runaway runs and push races |
| The prompt now says to push only to the checked-out branch | A guide for the agent, not an enforced limit |
